assessor: Assistant independent editorial review of complete actual Gemini outputs; not generator self-scoring, independent human panel review or application approval
ratingScale: 0 missing, 1 poor, 2 weak, 3 partial, 4 strong, 5 exceptional
methodology: Fresh run 05 uses the deadline-aware implementation recorded by source hashes. Actual shots, dialogue, graphics and HLNI were read in full; the unchanged weighted rubric was then applied. These are assistant editorial judgements with cited production evidence, not objective measurements, model self-scores or human content-owner approval. Source scripts were not manually revised. No institutional curriculum sources were supplied or independently verified.
runSummary: All three new Gemini drafts completed within 50 seconds: Trust 13,979 ms, Connection 7,977 ms, Discovery 11,239 ms. Each stayed Draft. All three attempted one advisory critique. Trust and Discovery returned validated rewrites; Connection retained its validated initial Draft after the advisory rewrite failed scene pacing. Full stage traces and rejected candidates are archived. Delivery succeeded for this single set; it does not establish statistical reliability or creative acceptance.
crossChannelFinding: The actual executions are more distinguishable than run 01: a three-column audit, a personal task journal and an evidence-card challenge. However, all remain mostly lone-student presentation. Trust demonstrates a better question without showing the preparation consequence; Connection confuses reading a liabilities row with a calculation and lacks a specific human decision; Discovery has a relevant evidence reveal but overstates what checking one handbook can establish. Different tool IDs and treatment labels are not proof of differentiation.
nextStep: CONTINUE PHASE 3A. Do not change the 85/100 threshold or advance to staging. Revise the specific missing consequence/term consistency/evidence scope in the actual writing process, then evaluate another separately authorized fresh set. Keep the deadline reservations and validated same-request Draft preservation; human semantic and factual review remain mandatory.

evidence.hlni: Shots 2–3 identify a known task (Analyze costs) and two genuinely missing fields, then ask what grading rubric is used. This is now a specific usable assessment-inquiry tool rather than asking for an already-known task. No degree-specific curriculum claim is made.
evidence.differentiation: The worksheet audit is distinct from the journal and card challenge, but the viewer still sees a lone student, desk and direct-address question. The explanation lacks enough academic depth and distinctive execution for the 4/5 differentiation floor.
evidence.coherence: The title-choice confusion leads to missing assessment information and an appropriate rubric question. Two printed task sheets in Shot 1 are never actually compared; the story becomes a single-task audit.
evidence.payoff: The resulting question follows from the empty criterion field. The story does not demonstrate how learning a criterion changes what the student prepares or how they compare B.Com/BBA options, so the asserted decision benefit is only partly earned.
evidence.production: Complete consecutive 6/12/10-second scenes with feasible paper props and concise speech. Graphic and dialogue repeat the sample; a natural read-aloud and phone legibility test remain pending.
evidence.originality: The audit is more operational than familiar course-title advice but keeps the repeated desk/paper/question execution.

assessments.automaticTriggerExplanation: No material falsehood or impossible production established. A meaningful bounded method is present. Revision is required by total and differentiation thresholds; academic sources and recorded production checks are still pending.
revisions: Use the unknown grading criterion to show a concrete preparation difference within a clearly labelled hypothetical example, or show two precise questions changing the original comparison method. Do not attribute invented criteria to either degree.
Connect the two initial task sheets to the actual investigation or remove unused props; retain the named degree decision at the consequence.
Make the value (what assessment information is missing) and payoff (what changes when checking it) distinct even if delivered in one exchange.

evidence.hlni: Shot 2 now inspects a sample balance sheet and records a specific sticking point: reading the Liabilities row. That supports a targeted teaching-support question, but Shot 3 instead asks how this calculation is taught. Reading a row and a calculation are not established as the same unknown.
evidence.differentiation: A first-person task journal provides a different tool from Trust and Discovery, but the solitary narrator remains a generic presenter. No particular friend/family pressure, confidence problem or concrete student decision develops.
evidence.coherence: The confusion-to-mini-task progression is connected, then the final question changes the academic problem from interpreting a label/row to a calculation that has not been shown.
evidence.payoff: The student becomes relieved and asks a question; no visible next action resolves a specific personal dilemma. The journal identifies a useful partial inquiry but does not fully earn its emotional resolution.
evidence.production: The delivered initial draft has complete feasible 6/9/13-second scenes. The attempted advisory rewrite was rejected for scene pacing; these scores concern the preserved initial draft only. The final 13-word on-screen question needs phone-size testing.
evidence.originality: The journal is specific enough to be less generic than motivational reassurance, but the blank-expression-to-relieved-presenter progression remains familiar.

assessments.automaticTriggerExplanation: No degree-specific factual assertion or impossible shot established. A partial meaningful inquiry method exists. The inconsistent final question and weak personal consequence fail HLNI, differentiation and total thresholds. The rejected rewrite is not being scored as the delivered output.
revisions: Keep the actual sticking point and resulting question identical in meaning: ask how students are taught to interpret that row, or visibly demonstrate the particular calculation first.
Build one believable personal choice that makes this method necessary and show what the student does differently afterward. A second actor is optional; human specificity is not.
Keep the bounded limit visible: one mini-task identifies a question; it does not predict aptitude or determine a degree choice.

evidence.hlni: The Strategy card has no source linking it to B.Com or BBA. Shot 2 correctly states insufficient information, teaching why an unlabeled business task cannot establish an exclusive degree classification. It avoids the unsupported both/neither answer.
evidence.differentiation: The card placement challenge, blank-card flip and missing-source reveal create a recognisably different curiosity experience from the worksheet and personal journal. Trendy is a chosen treatment, not a claim about a verified current trend.
evidence.coherence: B.Com/BBA remain the actual challenge subjects, and the missing source explains why the attempted classification fails. The ending narrows to required-task status, which is not identical to the opening question about belonging to a degree.
evidence.payoff: The third answer resolves the guessing game, but The only real question overstates the final handbook check. A task being required in one programme does not establish exclusivity or eliminate other relevant comparison questions.
evidence.production: Complete feasible 8/10/10-second scenes; the tablet Course Handbook interface is underspecified. It must be visibly a generic illustrative placeholder, not unverified official evidence. A phone legibility/read-aloud check is pending.
evidence.originality: The missing-evidence reversal is a useful small surprise, while detective props and stop-guessing advice remain familiar.

revisions: Replace the sole-question claim with a precise source request scoped to the named programme and current curriculum version; do not infer exclusivity from a single handbook.
